60148364.s: Al Abri Museum of Heritage and Classic Cars is one of the museums of the Al-Qassim region, in Riyadh Al Khabra Governorate. It was founded by Abdulrahman bin Nasser Al Abri. The museum consists of a main hall, two units, complete well-irrigation rigs and a large courtyard. The display includes a collection of heritage items such as weapons, coins, documents, hospitality and Arabic coffee utensils, old lighting tools, farming tools, old audio equipment, woodwork, leatherwork, palm-leaf crafts and some taxidermy animals. There is also an old kitchen and a bedroom with its original contents, while the courtyard holds the well rigs and a collection of old cars.

60148335.t: Antarah Ibn Shaddad Rock (Husat Al Nasla) in Ghaf Al Jiwa
60148335.s: Husat Al Nasla, or Antarah's Rock, is a red rock in the Al-Qassim region in central Saudi Arabia. It is one of the landmarks pointing to the story of Antarah ibn Shaddad and his cousin Abla, whose chapters unfolded between two rocks later known as Antar's rocks. The rock is one of the main sites on the approved tourist trail in Al-Qassim, a specialised trail among the literary-heritage trails of the region. The Saudi Commission for Tourism, with partners, carried out a number of introductory programmes and activities at the site, from Qusaiba in the northeast to the rock's location in Al Jiwa.

60148318.s: Maqsorat Alswailem is a large archaeological palace with annexes, built at the start of the 13th century AH during the time of the Emir of Al Bukayriyah, Abdullah bin Swailem bin Othman Al Swailem, after Al Bukayriyah Governorate was established. For a time it was the seat of the emirate, and received a number of kings and prominent figures, such as Imam Faisal bin Turki and King Abdulaziz when he came to Al Bukayriyah in 1325 AH. The Maqsorah is one of the most important heritage landmarks in Al Bukayriyah Governorate in the Al-Qassim region in central Saudi Arabia.

60148315.s: After Nasser Al Rajhi settled in Al Bukayriyah following many stops, the Maqsorah remains the physical trace of his journey. It was a duty to preserve and care for it so it would remain a prominent landmark in the heart of Al Bukayriyah. The Maqsorah has passed through many stages, with varying impact, from its founding until today, and it is now being developed and revitalised to take on a form and size suited to its heritage and historic setting.
60148315.b:
After Nasser Al Rajhi settled in Al Bukayriyah following many stops, the Maqsorah remains the physical trace of his journey. It was a duty to preserve and care for it so it would remain a prominent landmark in the heart of Al Bukayriyah. The Maqsorah has passed through many stages, with varying impact, from its founding until today, and it is now being developed and revitalised to take on a form and size suited to its heritage and historic setting.

The Maqsorah was built around 1190 AH after Nasser Al Rajhi moved from Al Hilaliyah. Different periods followed in which the rest of the main parts of the house were built: the mosque, the well and the coffee room.

60148285.b: Dar Al Ajdad Museum is one of the museums of the Al-Qassim region, in Ar Rass Governorate. It was founded by Daifallah Abdullah Mohammed Al Ghufaili. The museum is in a large traditional house with big halls, corridors and rooms, in which the heritage collection is displayed. The collection includes coffee tools, such as coffee pots that vary in make and size, kettles, coffee roasting pans, mortars and coffee grinders, as well as cooking utensils and vessels such as pots, trays, cauldrons and platters. There are also farming tools, such as ploughs and well-drawing gear, and a millstone for grinding and crushing grain. It also has some war equipment such as rifles, swords and spears, and a collection of clothing, jewellery and women's adornments. The museum also has a number of old cars displayed outside.

60148257.b:
Al Hamdan Museum is one of the museums of the Al-Qassim region, in Unaizah Governorate. It was founded by Ibrahim bin Saleh bin Hamad Al Hamdan. The museum is a large farm with many heritage buildings made of mud and mud brick and roofed with tamarisk wood. Its collection is displayed in the rooms of these buildings and in the passages between them in a well-organised way, hung on the wall, in aluminium display cases, on wooden stands or on shelves.

The museum's contents include men's and women's clothing, cooking, food and drink vessels, coffee vessels, lighting tools and incense burners, and a collection of war equipment and weapons including rifles, swords, daggers and spears, as well as farming and irrigation tools, some school supplies, books and manuscripts, and some coins. The display is sometimes used to portray certain trades and old family customs. In addition to the museum, the farm has a zoo with many kinds of domestic and tame wild animals, including predators.

60148254.s: Al Salhi Museum is one of the museums of the Al-Qassim region, in Unaizah Governorate. It was founded by Fahd Al Ali Al Salhi, and is a dilapidated mud house more than sixty years old, which Al Salhi bought at auction and turned into a museum within five months, preparing it for visitors and the interested public.
60148254.b: Al Salhi Museum is one of the museums of the Al-Qassim region, in Unaizah Governorate. It was founded by Fahd Al Ali Al Salhi, and is a dilapidated mud house more than sixty years old, which Al Salhi bought at auction and turned into a museum within five months, preparing it for visitors and the interested public. The museum has three floors on an area of 300 square metres. The first floor holds the folk majlis, the dome, the Al Maqlat and the courtyard, while the second floor has five rooms and balconies, all containing the furniture of an old Najdi home. The museum holds many heritage items and tools, including most of the tools of the old house as well as some used in farming, in the markets and elsewhere, along with old cars, coins and heritage books.

60148252.b: Mohammed Al Naim Museum is one of the museums of the Al-Qassim region, in Unaizah Governorate. It was founded by Mohammed Ibrahim Suleiman Al Naim. The museum is a traditional house with a concrete roof, made up of 4 rooms and an exhibition hall, covering all the activities of life and the needs of people at that time. In the middle of the museum are two halls, each with a traditional lamp, which also display a collection of heavy and large heritage pieces such as house doors, stone tools for grinding and pounding, and some farming tools such as the threshing sledge, the pulley and the plough.

60148249.s: Buraidah Museum is a museum in the city of Buraidah in the Al-Qassim region of Saudi Arabia that presents part of the region's heritage. It holds many items and has historical, scientific and cultural halls and a wing for the Aqeilat men, as well as a special wing for King Abdulaziz bin Abdul Rahman Al Saud with his private car, a folk heritage hall and a Saudi Aramco hall. Visitors can browse a number of published works on the city of Buraidah and the Al-Qassim region in the museum's library.

60148247.s: Aloqilat Museum preserves heritage pieces that tell the history the Al-Qassim region has been through over roughly the last 100 years, and is one of the private museums whose owners care about folk heritage.
60148247.b:
"Al-Aqili" or "Al-Aqeilat" is the name given to the tribes and families that traded in camels, horses, sheep and food. Aloqilat Museum preserves heritage pieces that tell the history the Al-Qassim region has been through over roughly the last 100 years. It is one of the private museums whose owners care about folk heritage and take care to collect distinctive heritage pieces and old cars, out of a principle of preserving heritage and keeping history for future generations.

The museum highlights the Aqeilat trade journeys, which set out from Al-Qassim and extended to Iraq, the Levant, Egypt, India and China. It also shows how the Aqeilat, through their journeys across history, helped carry Saudi culture to the countries they travelled to for trade.

In a fine building that echoes the old architectural style, the museum has a map of the route the Aqeilat took in travelling to the surrounding countries, as well as more than 100 panels documenting their history and many manuscripts and letters exchanged between the founding king (may God have mercy on him) and the Aqeilat in that period.

Visiting hours: the museum receives visitors from 8:30 am to 12:00 noon, and from 4:00 pm to 6:30 pm.

The museum is the work of Abdullatif Al Wuhaibi, who documented the history of the Aqeilat, one of the most famous modern trading journeys, which set out from the Al-Qassim region. Through the museum he founded on his own initiative and opened to visitors and researchers, he documented that history in photographs. The museum holds more than 10,000 historical documents on the Aqeilat, as well as their tools and a map of their trade routes. It includes most of the famous figures of the Aqeilat trade and the documents they used. The Aqeilat were a trading movement that set out from Najd, especially Al-Qassim, towards the lands bordering the Arabian Peninsula. It dates back about 300 years and ended with the demarcation of borders.
